question: Which PEP proposed making the CPython global interpreter lock optional?

subquestions: Which PEP is titled or describes making the CPython global interpreter lock (GIL) optional?

args.query: site:peps.python.org optional global interpreter lock PEP

observations.content:
[1] PEP 703 - Making the Global Interpreter Lock Optional in CPython | peps ...
    https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/
    The GIL is an obstacle to using multi-core CPUs from Python efficiently. This PEP proposes adding a build configuration (--disable-gil) to CPython to let it run Python code without the global interpreter lock and with the necessary changes needed to make the interpreter thread-safe. Motivation The GIL is a major obstacle to concurrency.

[2] PEP 703: Making the Python global interpreter lock optional
    https://lwn.net/Articles/919563/
    A new build configuration flag, --without-gil will be added to the configure script that will build CPython without the global interpreter lock. The posting of a PEP is only one step in a long path toward integrating this change into the CPython interpreter; expect some extended discussions over the coming months.

[3] PEP 703 - Making the Global Interpreter Lock Optional in CPython - GitHub
    https://github.com/irthomasthomas/undecidability/issues/733
    This PEP proposes adding a build configuration (--disable-gil) to CPython to let it run Python code without the global interpreter lock and with the necessary changes needed to make the interpreter thread-safe.

[4] PEP 703: Making the Python global interpreter lock optional
    https://lwn.net/Articles/919564/
    There is a section of the PEP that mentions runtime selection as a goal: This PEP introduces a new build mode (--without-gil) that is not ABI compatible with the standard build mode. The additional build mode adds complexity for both Python core developers and extension developers.

[5] What is PEP 703? | pydevtools
    https://pydevtools.com/handbook/explanation/what-is-pep-703/
    PEP 703: Making the Global Interpreter Lock Optional in CPython is the proposal that makes a no-GIL CPython build real. It adds a build configuration that removes the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), the mutex that lets only one thread execute Python bytecode at a time, producing the free-threaded Python interpreter.

    https://lwn.net/Articles/919563/
    Jan 10, 2023 · In late 2021, LWN covered a plan to eliminate the Python global interpreter lock (GIL), thus improving the language's thread-level concurrency. This plan has now been codified as PEP 703, which includes an extensive discussion of the changes that would be made.

[1] Global interpreter lock - Wikipedia
    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_interpreter_lock
    A global interpreter lock (GIL) is a mutual-exclusion lock held by a programming language interpreter thread to avoid sharing code that is not thread-safe with other threads. In implementations with a GIL, there is always one GIL for each interpreter process.

[2] PEP 703 – Making the Global Interpreter Lock Optional in CPython
    https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/
    CPython’s global interpreter lock (“GIL”) prevents multiple threads from executing Python code at the same time. The GIL is an obstacle to using multi-core CPUs from Python efficiently.

[3] PEP 703: Making the Python global interpreter lock optional [LWN.net]
    https://lwn.net/Articles/919563/
    The global interpreter lock will remain the default for CPython builds and python.org downloads. A new build configuration flag, --without-gil will be added to the configure script that will build CPython without the global interpreter lock.

[4] Python 3.14 will finally let us say goodbye to the Global Interpreter...
    https://www.linkedin.com/posts/foma-lim_python-314-will-finally-let-us-say-goodbye-activity-7382348024443867136-PpAi
    Python 3.14 introduces a significant development called free-threading, which allows disabling the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) as an opt-in mode. The GIL has been a core bottleneck for CPU-bound multi-threaded programs, since one thread could execute Python bytecode at a time.

[5] Python's Steering Council Plans to Make Its 'Global Interpreter Lock.....
    https://developers.slashdot.org/story/23/07/29/037250/pythons-steering-council-plans-to-make-its-global-interpreter-lock-optional
    Python's Global Interpreter Lock "allows only one thread to hold the control of the Python interpreter," according to the tutorial site Real Python. (They add, "it can be a performance bottleneck in CPU-bound and multi-threaded code.")

steps.note: The PEP that proposed making CPython’s **global interpreter lock (GIL) optional** is **PEP 703**: **“Making the Global Interpreter Lock Optional in CPython.”** ([S1])
